insights.content: DTC #1 won 4-1 over Spanish Trail #1 in W7 — clean as expected. Corelle dominated S1 6-2 6-1, Lobato won S2 6-2 6-1, Perdomo/Paull took D2 6-4 6-3, and Hernandez/Jarvis closed D3 6-2 6-4. The only blemish: Waters/Allen dropped D1 in a tiebreak (5-7 7-5 1-0) to VanPaepeghem/Sager from a team that's 1-5 on the season. That's a warning shot before W8 vs Red Rock #2.

Red Rock CC #2 leads 35B at 6-0 after sweeping DTC #3 5-0 in W7 — all five lines, no tiebreaks. DTC #1 is 5-1, Dragonridge is 4-2 (beat Desert Palm 4-1). The 35B title comes down to W8: DTC #1 vs Red Rock CC #2. A DTC #1 win makes it a one-match gap with four rounds to go; a loss puts Red Rock up 2 with 3 left and effectively hands them the division.

35A has a three-way logjam at the top. DTC #2 is 5-1 but had a W7 bye. Summerlin (5-2) and LTF (5-2) both won in W7 — Summerlin beat Anthem 3-2, LTF beat Red Rock #1 3-2. DTC #2 still holds the tiebreak edge, but if they drop one of their remaining two matches, Summerlin or LTF could sneak into first. 35A is a race to the wire.

Red Rock CC #2 is 6-0 and hasn't been seriously tested. Their W7 sweep used a mid-tier lineup — McAffee (3.34) at S1, Truman (3.58) at S2, and Watts (3.57)/MacDonald (3.72) at D1. Their top players (Toft 3.61, Chamberlain 3.61) were held back. Expect a full lineup for W8 against DTC #1. The depth at the top goes 5-6 players deep above 3.49.

Amy Waters (bl=3.66, r=3.58) and Emelia Allen (bl=3.68, r=3.57) are DTC #1's best weapon — but they just dropped a tiebreak at D1 to a Spanish Trail pair (VanPaepeghem bl=3.28 / Sager bl=3.50) from a 1-5 team. Red Rock's expected D1 is MacDonald (3.72)/Chamberlain or Watts (3.57)/MacDonald. Waters/Allen are competitive against any pair Red Rock deploys — but they can't afford a tiebreak loss there.

Stacie Corelle (bl=3.41, r=3.43) is playing her best tennis — 4-1 on the season at S1, including a comeback tiebreak win over Maria Allen in W6. She's DTC #1's most dangerous player by record. Red Rock's S1 option (Toft bl=3.54, r=3.61 or Chamberlain bl=3.56, r=3.61) is a tough assignment, but Corelle can compete. The singles lines are the hardest path for DTC #1 in W8.

sections.title: 5/9 — next match preview: DTC #1 vs RED ROCK CC #2

insights.content: DTC #1 (5-1) vs Red Rock CC #2 (6-0) — the 35B title match. Red Rock is the highest-rated roster in either subflight. MacDonald (bl=3.69, r=3.72), Toft (bl=3.54, r=3.61), Chamberlain (bl=3.56, r=3.61), Truman (bl=3.58, r=3.58), Watts (bl=3.49, r=3.57), Lind (bl=3.37, r=3.54). Six players rated 3.54 or above. DTC #1 is the underdog, but not dramatically at D1.

Put Waters/Allen at D1 — they're the best chance to steal a line from Red Rock. Corelle at S1 is the right call even against a strong opponent. Curtis/Hernandez or Hernandez/Perdomo at D2 gives depth. The goal is to win 3 lines: D1, D2, and one of the singles or D3. Avoid resting anyone — this is the match that decides the division.

DTC #1 wins 3-2 or loses 2-3. D1 is a toss-up. Singles are uphill. If Waters/Allen win D1 and Corelle steals S1 or S2, DTC #1 can take this. Red Rock's depth means every line is contested — don't expect any freebies.
vs RED ROCK CC #2 (6-0) — the season-defining match. Win and DTC #1 is in the driver's seat for first place. Lose and Red Rock leads by 2 with 3 left. DTC #1's most important match of the year.
vs SPANISH TRAIL #1 (1-5). Second meeting — DTC #1 won W1 5-0 against them. Even with the D1 stumble in W7, this is a comfortable win. Use it to rest top players if needed.

vs DRAGONRIDGE CC (4-2). Isbell (bl=3.04, r=3.33), Yarde (bl=3.52, r=3.54), and Gray (bl=3.53, r=3.52) make Dragonridge dangerous. DTC #1 won W6 3-2 in a competitive match. Expect another close one. Win here and DTC #1 finishes 7-3 minimum — a strong playoff position.

DTC #1 finishes top 2 in 35B with wins in W9 and W10, regardless of W8. A W8 win over Red Rock puts DTC #1 in contention for first and would be one of the best results in the division all season. The ceiling is high — the floor is a solid playoff seed.
